channel.title: Honolulu Civil Beat - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Honolulu Civil Beat (civilbeat.org)

item.title: Climate Funding Under New Hawai‘i Tax Could Be Cut By Millions
item.description: Legislation to instead charge a per-passenger fee would recoup less than half of all the green fee revenues cruise ships were expected to generate.

item.title: Denby Fawcett: My $54 Lesson In Social Media Scams
item.description: A bipartisan bill pending in Congress would require social media platforms to first verify a company’s business credentials before allowing it to advertise.

item.title: The Human Cost Of Waiting For Mental Health Care In Hawaiʻi
item.description: Long delays in access show up in families, in emergency rooms, and in communities across our state.

item.title: Honolulu Investigator Obstructed His Own Criminal Case, Hawaiʻi AG Says
item.description: The charges come after a Civil Beat report revealed Steve Alm's office knew about the allegations, botched an investigation and invited the employee back to work.

item.title: Is Now The Time For Reforming Hawaiʻi Schools?
item.description: A controversial bill would cut top superintendent positions from the DOE and increase community input in schools. Some families say the change is long overdue.

item.title: Word Search: Hawaiʻi Towns
item.description: Take a trip around the state with this word puzzle.

item.title: The Sunshine Blog: Sylvia Luke Is Still Talking About Her Own Political Mess
item.description: Short takes, outtakes, our takes and other stuff you should know about public information, government accountability and ethical leadership in Hawai‘i.

item.title: A Social Media Ban Won’t Make Hawaiʻi’s Keiki Safer
item.description: While the intent is understandable, the bill could produce unintended consequences for those it seeks to protect.

item.title: Controversial Kōloa Housing Project Gets Green Light In Unanimous Vote
item.description: Over objections, the commission cited the dire need for more homes. At least 45% of the units must go to locals.

item.title: Maui Planning Commission Rejects Bill To Save Thousands Of Vacation Rentals
item.description: The County Council would now need a supermajority vote to allow thousands of apartment-zoned units to keep operating as short-term rentals.
